description: We are sophomore students pursuing our interests in building creative and technical projects. We have a variety of skills ranging from programming and engineering to design and problem-solving.
summary:
SAFAR is a web tool designed to help mission planners and astronauts plan and carry out space walks on Mars․ SAFAR was developed using data from a 4․44 × 4․44 km grid in the Jezero Crater region of Mars‚ where NASA's Perseverance rover is active․ Elevation data for SAFAR development were acquired with the HiRISE camera on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter․

SAFAR produces a grade and cost map using elevation information․ SAFAR produces three trip plans: minimum risk‚ minimum time‚ and science‚ including user-selected science stops․ SAFAR provides information about oxygen and battery use for the trip plans and filters out infeasible trip plans based on oxygen and battery limitations․ SAFAR tracks oxygen and battery use‚ weather conditions‚ and distance traveled during an excursion and tells the astronaut when to turn back․ SAFAR shares excursion information with mission control․

Our issue is exploring Mars's surface․ Limited supplies of oxygen and other materials will limit explorers' movement on Mars․ Other risks associated with exploring unknown and possibly dangerous terrain exist․ SAFAR offers an integrated tool that can help explorers answer three questions: In which direction should we go? Will we have the necessary supplies to reach our destination? When should we return?
details:
What it does and how it works

SAFAR covers the whole walk in four steps: plan, compare, navigate and monitor. Five connected workspaces share one live mission: Plan, Navigate, Mission Control, Environment and Science.

  1. Real terrain. A Python pipeline downloads one HiRISE stereo elevation model from the NASA Planetary Data System (product DTEEC_048842_1985_048908_1985_U01), plus its matching orthoimage.
    • It fetches only the 3.5 MB it needs out of a 411 MB product.
    • It builds a 201 × 201 routing grid at 22 m spacing. All 40,401 cells passed validation, with no gaps filled in.
    • Every file is checksummed, so the data is reproducible offline.
    • Events like an approaching dust front or a sudden loss of oxygen raise alerts.
    • SAFAR automatically advises the crew to turn back before their margins run out.
    • An alert stays visible until the condition is actually resolved, even after someone acknowledges it.
  2. Mission control. Operators see the same mission state: crew status, the elevation profile and alert history.

Benefits and impact

  • Safety first: SAFAR refuses to plan a walk the suit can't support.
  • One shared view: the astronaut and mission control look at the same mission, which cuts down miscommunication.
  • Honest data: every number is tagged as Real, Derived or Simulated, with its source, so users know what to trust.
  • Easy to try: no install, login or server is needed; it runs in a web browser on desktop or phone.
  • Long-term goal: a planning and training tool for future crewed Mars missions, and a teaching tool that shows the public how real orbital data supports exploration.

Tools and technologies

  • App: TypeScript, React 19, Vite, React Router, Zustand and TanStack Query.
  • 3D terrain: Three.js with React Three Fiber, using WebGPU where available, then WebGL 2, then a 2D map.
  • Interface: Radix UI and Lucide icons.
  • Data pipeline: Python scripts that prepare the HiRISE elevation and imagery.
  • Testing: Vitest (33 unit tests), Playwright (8 end-to-end browser tests), and axe-core accessibility checks against the WCAG 2.1 AA standard.
  • NASA data: the HiRISE stereo elevation model and orthoimage from the NASA Planetary Data System (University of Arizona and USGS).

What makes it creative

  • Most Mars maps only show the terrain. SAFAR turns the terrain into a decision: which route to take, whether the crew can afford it, and when to turn back.
  • It brings path planning and resource budgeting from robotics into a mission tool that people can actually use.
  • The rover's crater becomes a practice ground for future astronauts.

Factors we considered

  • Safety and honesty: suit drain, walking speed, weather, radiation, and the habitat and science-site locations are simulated, and the app labels them clearly. The routes are not certified for real astronaut safety.
  • Accuracy: we used real, validated NASA data without filling any gaps.
  • Accessibility: full keyboard control, reduced-motion support and accessibility testing.
  • Device reach: it works on phones, and the 3D view falls back step by step down to a 2D map on older hardware.
  • Offline use: a static app with checksummed data.
  • Next NASA datasets: we've designed adapters (not yet built in) for Mars 2020 MEDA weather, Mars 2020 SPICE (Perseverance's actual route), the PIXL, SHERLOC and SuperCam instruments for science targets, NASA SWIM subsurface ice, and MOLA regional terrain.
